1.title: Microsoft Foundry: Resources, Models and the Portal
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Microsoft Foundry: Resources, Models and the Portal. It covers the exam area Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. What Microsoft Foundry is. The Foundry portal. Deploy a model in the portal. Chat with the model: the playground. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (fifty-five to sixty percent). Exam format: a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes; check the exam page for the time. Validated against: the official A I nine oh one study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: What Microsoft Foundry is
1.text: What Microsoft Foundry is. Microsoft Foundry is Microsoft's platform to build A I agents, models and apps. It "unifies agents, models and tools under a single management grouping". It was called Azure A I Foundry and, before that, Azure A I Studio; Azure A I Services became Foundry Tools.

1.title: What Microsoft Foundry is, continued
1.text: What Microsoft Foundry is. Foundry resource. The Azure resource that holds your A I setup (one resource, with projects). Project. A place to organize your work: it contains models, agents and other resources your team uses. Model catalog. The list of models you can deploy. Foundry Tools. Prebuilt services: Language, Speech, Vision, Content Understanding. Foundry portal. The web portal (ai.azure.com) to deploy models, chat, build agents and manage the project.

1.title: What Microsoft Foundry is, continued
1.text: What Microsoft Foundry is. The figure shows this: A Foundry resource contains projects; a project holds model deployments and agents.

1.title: What Microsoft Foundry is, continued
1.text: What Microsoft Foundry is. Each project has an endpoint that your code uses, in this form: H T T P S colon slash slash resource name dot services dot ai dot azure dot com slash api slash projects or project name. Exam tip: Resource equals the Azure container. Project equals your workspace inside it, with the models and agents you use. Code connects to the project endpoint.

1.title: The Foundry portal
1.text: The Foundry portal. The portal has a "New Foundry" experience. Main areas named in the quickstarts. Build. Catalog (model catalog), Models (your deployments), Agents. Manage. Project details, users and access. Playgrounds. Try a model or an agent without writing code. You need an Azure subscription and permission to create the resource. To let others work in the project, give them access under Manage.

1.title: Deploy a model in the portal
1.text: Deploy a model in the portal. Steps (as in the quickstart). Open the portal and your project. Go to Build to Catalog to Model catalog. Search for a model (for example G P T five mini ). Select Deploy to Default settings (or custom settings). Note the deployment name (for example G P T five mini ).

1.title: Deploy a model in the portal, continued
1.text: Deploy a model in the portal. The figure shows this: Five portal steps from the catalog to a deployed model.

1.title: Deploy a model in the portal, continued
1.text: Deploy a model in the portal. The deployment is what your code and the playground call. It has a name, a model and a deployment type (Module three). For most workloads, start with Global Standard. You are billed for what you use, so delete deployments you no longer need. Exam tip: The resource is the Azure container, the project is your workspace inside it, and code connects to the project endpoint.

1.title: Chat with the model: the playground
1.text: Chat with the model: the playground. After you deploy, you land in the model playground. Type messages and read replies: a chat you can try at once. Edit the system prompt (Module six). Configure parameters: temperature, top p, max tokens (Module three). Attach tools to test them: web search, file search, code interpreter. Compare mode lets you test up to three models side by side. Guardrails (content safety settings) can be adjusted. There is also an agents playground for agents (Module nine). Exam tip: "Test a deployed model without writing code" to playground. "Compare two models on the same prompt" to compare mode. "Change how random the answers are" to temperature.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants a place that holds the models and agents its team uses for one solution. What should it create in Microsoft Foundry? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A project. A Foundry project organizes the models, agents and other resources a team uses.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A developer wants to try a deployed model with different system prompts before writing code. Where? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The model playground in the Foundry portal. The playground is for chatting with a deployed model and changing prompts and parameters.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which is the first step to find a model to deploy in the portal? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Go to Build, then the model catalog, and search for the model. Deployment starts in the model catalog under Build.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which value does application code use to connect to a Foundry project? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The project endpoint. Code connects through the project endpoint.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. What name did Microsoft Foundry have before? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Azure A I Foundry. Azure A I Foundry (and earlier Azure A I Studio) became Microsoft Foundry.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which feature lets a team test the same prompt against up to three models at once? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Compare mode. The playground has a compare mode for up to three models.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the portal address for Foundry? Answer: ai.azure.com. Question two. What does a Foundry project contain? Answer: Models, agents and other resources the team uses. Question three. What is the deployment type to start with for most workloads? Answer: Global Standard.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What are the Build area's parts for your work? Answer: Catalog, Models and Agents. Question five. What was Azure A I Services renamed? Answer: Foundry Tools. Question six. What does the playground let you adjust? Answer: System prompt, parameters such as temperature, tools and guardrails.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Foundry: platform for agents, models, tools; formerly Azure A I Foundry and Azure A I Studio. Resource and project: resource holds projects; project holds models and agents; code uses the project endpoint. Portal: ai.azure.com; Build (catalog, models, agents); Manage (project details, users). Deploy: Build, Catalog, search, Deploy, default settings, note the deployment name; start with Global Standard. Playground: chat, system prompt, parameters, tools, compare up to three models, guardrails. In the next module, we continue the course.
